title: Prompt Failure Inventory and Annotator Contract: Scenario Taxonomy & Labeling Protocol
author: Morgan Reyes
body:
Summary
This document defines a reproducible taxonomy of prompt-level failure modes, a recommended scenario-driven inventory format, and a labeling contract for human annotators and automated heuristics. It is intended for evaluation teams, model-onboarding engineers, and regression triage owners who need consistent, high-quality labels that link prompt characteristics to observable model behaviors.

Goals and scope
- Create a small, stable set of failure categories that cover production-relevant errors (not every linguistic edge case).
- Standardize the prompt + context metadata we store for each failure (the inventory manifest).
- Provide a clear annotator contract and decision rules so labels are consistent across raters and over time.
- Enable automated triage heuristics to bootstrap labels and prioritize human review when confidence is low.

Intended audience
- Applied ML engineers running eval harnesses
- Model onboarding reviewers who must certify promotion readiness
- Regression triage teams performing root-cause analysis
- Annotation leads and quality control managers

High-level taxonomy (first-class categories)
1) Incorrect factual response (FactError)
- Model asserts verifiably false facts about current or historical reality.
- Example triggers: wrong dates, wrong numerical facts, incorrect entity attributes.

2) Hallucinated entity or citation (Hallucination)
- Model invents an entity, citation, or document that cannot be substantiated by the provided context or a reasonable external check.

3) Instruction misinterpretation (InstructionMismatch)
- Model fails to follow explicit instructions in the prompt (wrong format, omitted fields, reversed order).

4) Safety policy violation (Safety)
- Model produces content that violates safety constraints: disallowed instructions, harassment, PII leakage, or actionable wrongdoing.

5) Degraded semantic relevance (RelevanceDrop)
- Output drifts off-topic, becomes generic, or ignores context dependencies (e.g., ignores prior chat turns).

6) Tokenization/formatting breakage (FormatError)
- Output contains broken JSON, truncated code blocks, or malformed special tokens causing downstream parser failures.

7) Quantization/artifact degradation (QuantArtifact)
- Output shows artefacts consistent with quantization or KV-cache instability: repeated phrases, tokenization hallucinations, or inconsistent scalar outputs across repeats.

8) Latency/partial-output fallbacks (LatencyFallback)
- Model response indicates it timed out, returned partial content, or used fallback model variant with degraded quality.

Inventory manifest: required fields
Use this manifest layout for every logged failure. Store as a row in the failure catalog (CSV/Parquet/JSONL).
- prompt_id: Unique stable id for prompt fixture (example: pf_2026_00021)
- source: Origin of prompt (prod/bench/manual/synthetic) (example: prod:search-assist)
- seed_text: The raw prompt text (truncated to 8k chars) (example: "Summarize the following...")
- context_snapshot: Short context hash or description of conversation state (example: chat:session_241)
- model_version: Exact model + flavor used (example: gpt-redwood-v2-quant8)
- hardware_profile: deployment type (hosted/dedicated/private) + instance (example: dedicated:p4d-32gb)
- timestamp_utc: ISO8601 of the run (example: 2026-01-12T20:34:22Z)
- failure_category: One of taxonomy labels (example: Hallucination)
- severity: low/medium/high (see severity guidelines) (example: high)
- repeatability: always/sometimes/rare (example: sometimes)
- annotator_id: human rater or automated heuristic id (example: annot-v2-17)
- confidence_score: 0.0-1.0 (string for JSON flatness) (example: 0.82)
- reproduction_steps: Minimal steps to reproduce; include seeds and flags (example: see reproduction_notes)
- related_run_ids: Other run ids for cross-comparison (example: [run_123, run_124])

Severity guidelines
- High: visible user harm or complete feature break (Safety, pervasive FactError that changes user action).
- Medium: materially degrades UX or model correctness but has a straightforward workaround (RelevanceDrop, FormatError).
- Low: cosmetic or rare issues tolerated by product (minor hallucination on non-critical content).

Annotator contract: decision rules and procedures
1) Single-pass automated triage (pre-labeling)
  a) Run deterministic heuristics: entity-checker against knowledge base, JSON-parse validator for FormatError, safety classifier.
  b) If heuristics produce confidence >= 0.9 and unanimous category, set label = automated value and set annotator_id = auto:<heuristic>.
  c) Otherwise, queue for human review.

2) Human annotation workflow
  1) "Read the prompt and produced output verbatim, then consult the context_snapshot if provided."
  2) "Apply the taxonomy: choose the single best category. If multiple categories apply, select primary by impact to user (safety > fact > relevance)."
  3) "Write a one-sentence justification in the free-text justification field for auditability."
  4) "Assign severity and repeatability using the guidance above."
  5) "If unsure, mark label 'needs_discuss' and add required evidence (e.g., external fact links)."

3) Adjudication rules (when annotator disagreement >= 2 raters disagree)
- Triage to an adjudicator pool. Adjudicator applies evidence-gathering protocol: web lookup, cross-model comparison, and consults model-onboarding lead. Final label must include a short evidentiary note.

Inter-annotator agreement (IAR) targets and sampling
- Initial onboarding target: Cohen's kappa >= 0.6 on a 500 example calibration set.
- Production maintenance: sample 1% of daily labeled items (min 50) for IAR monitoring; investigate drift if kappa drops below 0.55.

Automation heuristics and feature checklist for bootstrap labeling
- Exact-match referent check (KB lookup): flags FactError/Hallucination.
- JSON/markup health check: flags FormatError.
- Safety classifier (ensemble of policy and regex): candidate Safety.
- N-gram repetition and perplexity delta tests: candidate QuantArtifact.
- Context similarity score: candidate RelevanceDrop if low similarity.

Data retention and privacy notes
- Do not store full PII in the manifest; if prompts may contain PII, store a redacted_seed_text and reference to secure vault for retrieval under approved workflows.
- Retention default: 90 days for full text in the eval environment, 3 years for redacted manifest entries. Follow security-and-compliance/data-management policies for customer data.

Integration with eval harness and triage pipelines
- Naming conventions: prompt fixtures used by the eval harness should include fixture_id matching prompt_id in the manifest.
- When a new failure is logged, the harness should attach: trace_id, cost_metrics (tokens, latency), and model-runtime snapshot to the manifest.
- Provide a stable API endpoint for the triage dashboard to stream new manifest entries (schema URL: /internal/eval-manifest/v1).

Operational playbook: from failure detection to remediation
1) Detection: auto-heuristics mark candidate failures and assign confidence.
2) Prioritization: failures are ranked by severity x user-impact metric (e.g., active sessions affected).
3) Human review: annotators label top N for the day where N is set by SRE/product trust thresholds.
4) Root-cause analysis: triage uses model_version diffs, quant profiles, and workload fingerprints to hypothesize cause.
5) Remediation: roll forward/rollback, quant profile adjustments, prompt-template patches, or retraining tasks.
6) Postmortem: document actions, mitigation latency, and regression test additions.

Sample labeling example (annotator checklist)
- Prompt id: pf_2026_00021
- Raw prompt (redacted): "List the founding year of OpenCo and provide citations."
- Model output: "OpenCo was founded in 2008. See Journal of AI, 2009."
- Quick checks: KB lookup suggests founding year is 2012 -> FactError, severity=medium, repeatability=sometimes. Justification: "Founding year mismatch with public registry (link provided)."

Metrics and dashboards to expose
- Failure rate per 1000 prompts by category (rolling 7d)
- Median time-to-label for queued items (goal < 6 hours for high severity)
- IAR trendline and adjudication backlog size
- Cross-model delta matrix: how frequently a failure appears in variant pairs (useful for quant causality)

Governance and lifecycle
- The taxonomy is intentionally small. We will revisit quarterly. Any proposal to add a new top-level category requires a 2/3 vote from applied-ml, model-onboarding, and product trust leads.
- Maintain an examples corpus of ~2k labeled prompts (balanced across categories) used for annotator onboarding and heuristic tuning.

Appendix A: quick-reference decision flow
- heuristics confident? -> auto-label -> persist
- heuristics low confidence -> human queue -> label/adjudicate -> persist
- severity high -> escalate to oncall/model-owner and attach replication bundle

Appendix B: recommended JSON schema snippet for the manifest (single-row example)
{
  "prompt_id": "pf_2026_00021",
  "source": "prod:chat-assist",
  "seed_text": "[REDACTED]",
  "model_version": "gpt-redwood-v2-quant8",
  "failure_category": "FactError",
  "severity": "medium"
}

Contacts and ownership

- Secondary reviewers: Nadia Chen (model-onboarding), Aakash Patel (eval-harness)
- Adjudication pool: annot-leads@redwood-inference.internal
